title: Lemon Ricotta Pancakes
changes_from_base: Ricotta and milk replace the buttermilk and soured cream, the batter is flavoured with lemon sugar, and the egg whites are whisked to a meringue and folded in for extra lift.
summary: Light, cloud-like pancakes with the gentle zing of lemon and the richness of ricotta, finished with a golden crust.
equipment: stand mixer with whisk (or electric hand mixer)
wire rack set in a rimmed baking tray
nonstick frying pan (30 cm) or griddle

ingredients.note: 1 tbsp rubbed with the zest, the rest whisked into the whites

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt
unsalted butter, plus more to serve
fresh fruit or compote, to serve

steps.title: Zest and whisk
steps.text: Rub 15 g caster sugar and 1 tsp finely grated lemon zest together with your fingers until fragrant (about 30 s). Whisk 226 g whole-milk ricotta, 180 ml whole milk, 4 large egg yolks, ½ tsp vanilla and the lemon sugar.

steps.title: Dry mix
steps.text: Sift 141 g plain flour, 1 tsp baking powder and ¼ tsp fine salt into the ricotta mixture and whisk until just combined.

steps.title: Whip whites
steps.text: Whisk 4 large egg whites on medium until foamy (about 1 min), slowly add 30 g caster sugar and whisk to glossy medium-stiff peaks (about 5 min); fold into the batter.

steps.title: Set up and cook
steps.text: Set a wire rack in a rimmed baking tray. Heat a griddle to medium (175 °C) or a frying pan over medium heat; melt ½ tbsp unsalted butter and scoop 80 ml portions to make 8 cm pancakes (1-2.5 cm apart). Cook until bubbles appear and the base is golden (2-3 min); flip and cook until golden and cooked through (2-4 min). Move to the rack and repeat.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve warm with fresh fruit or compote and maple syrup.

tips: Separating the eggs allows the beaten whites to create an airy, soufflé-like texture when folded through the batter.
A griddle heated to 175 °C gives more even cooking than stovetop alone; if using a pan, adjust the heat so the base turns golden without over-browning.
Cook the batter soon after folding in the whites, while it is still light and airy.
storage: Best served fresh and warm. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
